picks.name: The Sustainability Buyer
picks.why_plausible: The brief's core claim is recycled ocean plastic, and this persona makes decisions on environmental footprint and buys sustainable_apparel at a typical AOV of $92, matching the ~$90 first order. Price sensitivity medium is fine at this tier.
lean_into: specific sustainability claims — recycled ocean plastic as the fabric source
material transparency about what the garment is made of
avoid: vague eco claims like 'good for the planet'
anything that reads as fast fashion or seasonal drops
unverified certification claims the brand hasn't stated
picks.ad_angle: The material story: ocean plastic recovered and spun into the fabric you train in — concrete, not vague eco talk.

picks.name: The Fitness Enthusiast
picks.why_plausible: Works out 4+ times a week and buys performance apparel with low-medium price sensitivity; the brand explicitly values performance and sits in the premium activewear tier. Activewear is their top category affinity.
lean_into: gear that holds up to frequent training
avoid: athlete endorsement claims the brief doesn't support
picks.ad_angle: Performance first: technical activewear that survives four-plus sessions a week — sustainability is a bonus, not an excuse.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: Female, 28-40, treats her body as a system and pays premiums for considered products; fitness and wellness are both scored interests in the brief. Low price sensitivity with a $95 AOV matches the $90 first order.
lean_into: transparency about what the product is made of
avoid: pseudo-scientific claims the brief can't back
picks.ad_angle: Your kit as part of the routine: the one wardrobe upgrade for a woman who already optimizes sleep, training and food.

picks.name: The Affluent Classic
picks.why_plausible: Female, low price sensitivity, $145 AOV, and values quality and longevity over trends — the premium price point between Lululemon and Girlfriend Collective supports a durability pitch. Apparel and self-treat are her scored overlaps.
picks.ad_angle: Quiet quality: pieces made well enough to keep for years, in a category that usually asks you to replace them.

plan.summary: Two activewear sellers (Movewell, Cloudfoot) are competitors, so the plan rests on a sustainability-aligned footwear test (Stride & Stem) and fitness-services traffic at Studiogrid, with women's apparel publishers as lower-conviction tests where the audience skews older than the 25-44 target.

test.name: Stride & Stem

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: 94% female; high income for premium price

test.adjustment_reason: Notes state 'Sustainability and machine-washable claims resonate', a direct match to the recycled-ocean-plastic story that the 50 values score underweights.
test.rationale: Stride & Stem's 94% female professional buyers already respond to sustainability claims, making it the cleanest values match in the catalog for recycled ocean plastic; footwear only lightly overlaps activewear.
test.risk: Only 3.2M monthly impressions, so volume will be thin even if conversion is strong.

test.name: Studiogrid

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: 74% female; high income for premium price

test.adjustment_reason: Notes say users are 'actively spending on self-care and fitness', a post-class buying moment that the category score (50) understates for activewear.
test.rationale: Studiogrid books fitness classes and spa appointments for a 74% female, high-income audience, so the confirmation page catches women right after committing to a workout habit; notes confirm they are 'actively spending on self-care and fitness'.

evidence.quote: Users are actively spending on self-care and fitness

test.risk: Service bookings at $42 are a different purchase mindset than a $90 apparel order, so click-to-buy may lag.

test.name: Marlowe & Co.

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: 96% female; high income for premium price

test.adjustment_reason: Audience age_skew 45-65 sits well outside the brand's stated 25-44 range, and notes flag 'Lower impulse', which the 100 audience score ignores.
test.rationale: Marlowe & Co. delivers affluent women at a $112 AOV, but they are 45-65 and respond to 'quality messaging' rather than the workout-performance angle this brand leads with.

evidence.quote: Older affluent women. Lower impulse but high AOV

test.risk: Age mismatch with a 25-44 activewear brand; sustainability story may not drive this cohort.

test.name: Everbody

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: 99% female; mid income for premium price

test.adjacent_conflict: sells intimates, womens_apparel, a close substitute
test.rationale: Everbody's 99% female shoppers at an $89 AOV match the price point exactly, and its 'fit-focused messaging' orientation suits activewear — provided the brand actually offers inclusive sizing.

evidence.quote: Audience values representation and fit-focused messaging

test.risk: Mid-income plus-size audience may balk at a premium price, and a narrow size range would read badly here.

test.name: Linden Park

signals.name: audience
signals.detail: 98% female; high income for premium price

test.adjustment_reason: Audience age_skew of 50-70 plus a 'Conservative brand sensibility' is a poor match for a 25-44 sustainable activewear brand, which the 100 audience score misses.
test.rationale: Linden Park has the catalog's highest apparel AOV, but its 50-70 classic-workwear buyer is two decades older than the target and its conservative sensibility clashes with ocean-plastic positioning.
test.risk: Oldest audience in the plan; activewear relevance and sustainability messaging both likely to underperform.

bid_strategy.rationale: $90 first order × 0.30 = $27.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: We assumed a first order around $90 based on the named comparison brands.
We assumed buyers are mostly women aged 25-44.
We assumed one-time purchases rather than a subscription.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher cleared the recommended bar, so the whole budget is a test. Treat results as exploratory.
